messages:
andrew: Ran a perfetto capture on the new multi-arch scratch build and line info is basically gone for our kernels. timeline shows big GPU bursts but stacks are just addresses. Anyone seen this after switching base image?

mica: huh, did the binary get stripped or are debug sections relocated? scratch images often lose the /usr/lib/.build-id store.

andrew: binary was built on CI x86 host, then copied into an arm64 runtime image for testing (qemu user). we didn't strip, but the container has no build-id dir. sample from perfetto: 
```
GPU kernel 0x7f8a1b3c -> <addr 0x7f8a1b3c> (no symbol)
CPU frame 0x400d9e -> <addr 0x400d9e> (no line)
```

andrew: I also tried nvprof and it shows mangled names but no source lines. nvprof output attached: https://redwood.safe/attach/ci/19321/nvprof.txt

sanjay: two likely culprits: (1) build-id / pathmap mismatch in container, (2) CUPTI agent version and in-container CUDA tooling mismatch. When CUPTI can't find debug data it reports addresses only.

mica: ^ this. check that .note.gnu.build-id from the host-built binary matches what's available in the container under /usr/lib/debug/.build-id or /usr/lib/.build-id. Also check if objcopy --only-keep-debug was used or not.

andrew: how do we check quickly?

sanjay: run: `readelf -n bin/redwood-runtime | grep GNU` and `eu-readelf -n` if you have elfutils. Also `build-id --verify` lol. simpler: `curl -sS --unix-socket /proc/1/fd/0 http://` jk. but really `readelf -n bin/redwood-runtime` shows the note.

ops: perf-bot: perf job 78231 finished: perfetto trace uploaded to https://perfetto.local/traces/78231 (size 28MB) :white_check_mark:

mica: another quick repro: run the container with the host's /usr/lib/debug mounted and re-run perfetto. If symbols appear, it's a build-id mapping problem.

andrew: tried that and got partial lines back for CPU frames but GPU kernels still unresolved. output: `cupti: agent found, but kernel debug index missing` in CUPTI logs.

sanjay: GPU kernels need two things: (A) the PTX/CUBIN mapping available to CUPTI, (B) the host-side cupti library version compatible with driver. If we cross-build, the cubin objects embedded might be stripped. check `cuobjdump --dump-sass` on the container build.

andrew: run `cuobjdump -sass bin/model_kernel.cubin` gives assembly but no source file mapping. maybe our build pipeline `-g` for nvcc isn't producing relocatable debug info inside cubin when using `-lineinfo`?

mica: nvcc flag is `-lineinfo` and `-G` for device debugging, but `-G` disables optimizations. Usually we use `-lineinfo` + `-g` host. Also ensure `--generate-line-info` for the newer toolchains.

andrew: FYI build pipeline snippet: 
```
NVCCFLAGS += -O3 -lineinfo
CXXFLAGS += -g -fdebug-prefix-map=$(SRC)=/redwood/src
strip --strip-debug ? not used in CI
```

mica: That debug-prefix-map might be the issue: perfetto sees /redwood/src/... which doesn't exist in container. Either embed a pathmap or keep the original sources under the same paths or strip/replace with correct prefix using `objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink`.

sanjay: also check CUPTI environment: we had one case where LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointed to host libcupti.so while container had different driver => CUPTI returned limited metadata. set `CUptiActivityEnable=1` and capture its logs: `export CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL=1 CUPTI_LOG=1` then re-run.

andrew: re-ran with `CUPTI_LOG=4` and saw warnings about `unable to find cubin debug info for module id 0x12`.

ops: perf-bot: debug job queued to run `rebuild-with-debug` pipeline.

mica: possible quick workaround: use addr2line with the host binary and map GPU symbols by address range reported in perfetto. Ugly but works for quick triage. `addr2line -e bin/redwood-runtime 0x400d9e`.

andrew: did that, CPU lines resolved. For GPU I used `cuobjdump --list-sources` and mapped kernel offsets -> source lines. Could be automated in our trace postprocessor.

sanjay: long term: add a step in release pipeline to `--build-id` preserve and push `debug` objects into a debugstore that perfetto collector can query, or mount `/usr/lib/debug` in the private test images. Also ensure CUPTI and driver versions are pinned to the same minor version.

andrew: thanks. next actions: 1) re-run with host /usr/lib/debug mounted (in progress), 2) re-run with CUPTI_LOG=4 and attach logs (in progress), 3) try building cubin with `-G` and `-lineinfo` in a debug variant to see mapping (queued).

mica: add a note to the perf run ticket to record which container image and which driver were used (driver mismatches are silent killers).

andrew: will do. posting logs here when available. :thumbsup:
